part1.name: Elastic limit conserves energy
part1.what: No adhesion, no damping, no plasticity: restitution must be 1.

part1.name: Viscoelastic damping calibration
part1.what: Non-adhesive impact must reproduce the material's dry restitution e_dry = 0.85.

part1.name: Plastic restitution (Thornton & Ning 1998)
part1.what: Elastic-plastic impacts must follow the analytic Thornton-Ning restitution.

part1.name: Plasticity with damping
part1.what: With realistic damping (e_dry = 0.7) plastic impacts must give ~ e_TN x e_dry (no damping of a separated contact).

part1.name: Outcome depends only on impact energy
part1.what: Same 1/2 m v^2 with twice the mass must give the same restitution (dimensional analysis of the contact law).

part1.name: Sticking threshold limits
part1.what: Without damping the DEM threshold equals the JKR hysteresis energy estimate; grains stick below / bounce above it; carbon stickier than silica.
part1.value: undamped 3.825 vs JKR 3.827 mm/s; damped silica 6.18 mm/s

part1.name: Free flight with gas drag
part1.what: Residual acceleration + drag vs the exact analytic trajectory over 1 s.

part1.name: Spinning payload frame (Coriolis + centrifugal + drag)
part1.what: Grain trajectory vs a 1e-12-tolerance ODE solution: exact at 1 rpm, 2nd-order convergence at 30x spin.
part1.value: 1 rpm: 0.279 nm; 0.5 Hz: 26.76 um, convergence ratio 4.00

part1.name: Free rotation of an aggregate
part1.what: Spinning linear trimer in vacuum for 5 s: angular momentum conserved; the rotational-energy error (sampled every step) stays bounded and does not drift.

part1.name: Rigid-body collision impulse
part1.what: 200 random oblique impacts on a trimer: post-impact normal velocity = -e v_n exactly; friction stays inside the Coulomb cone.

part1.name: Momentum through sticking and fragmentation
part1.what: Merging three grains into an aggregate and splitting one off conserve linear and angular momentum.

part1.name: Vibrating walls never let grains out
part1.what: 150 grains (forming spinning aggregates) against 25 um / 200 Hz vibrating walls for 1 s: no grain surface may cross a wall, and the position safety net must never be needed.
part1.value: worst penetration = 0.00 nm over 501 wall bounces (0 safety-net corrections)

part1.name: No missed collisions in a dense gas
part1.what: 300 grains in a 6 mm box for 0.5 s: at the end of every step no two separate bodies may interpenetrate.
part1.value: worst overlap = 0.0e+00 R over 286 grain-grain impacts

part1.name: Long-range electrostatics (Ewald mesh)
part1.what: Short-range pairs + grounded-box particle-mesh field vs Coulomb's law, and the image force near a grounded wall.

part1.name: Contact charging saturates
part1.what: Repeated wall contacts drive the grain to the potential that cancels the work-function difference.

part1.name: Sticking-threshold estimator
part1.what: Logistic fit + bootstrap on synthetic impacts with a known 30 mm/s threshold: unbiased, robust to perfectly separated data; the coverage of its 1-sigma intervals is reported (nominal 68%).

part1.name: Spin in the spinning payload frame
part1.what: A spinning grain, and an L-shaped aggregate 5 cm off the spin axis, in vacuum for 10 s at 1 rpm about a tilted axis: their absolute angular momentum must stay fixed in inertial space (so it appears to precess at -Omega in the chamber); centrifugal force must not torque the aggregate.

part1.name: Impacts never create energy
part1.what: Every impact, measured just before and after it is resolved: grains hitting spinning chains and L-shaped aggregates at 0.02-3 m/s from random directions and offsets, spinning aggregates hitting a wall, and 0.5 s of a closed box of 300 spinning graphite grains. Kinetic energy plus the energy of broken bonds may never increase, and no aggregate may keep grains that no longer touch.
part1.value: max gain +1.0e-13 of the impact energy over 1169 impacts (95 with fragmentation); phantom bonds 0

part1.name: Friction never creates energy
part1.what: 2000 random eccentric impacts on an aggregate with friction (where rigid-body friction laws can gain energy): every impulse must dissipate.

part1.name: Gas drag limits (Stokes / Epstein)
part1.what: The slip-corrected drag must reduce to Stokes drag in dense gas and to Epstein free-molecular drag (diffuse reflection) at low pressure.
part1.details: The empirical slip correction sits ~2.5% below ideal diffuse-reflection Epstein drag.

part1.name: Thermophoresis vs the standard free-molecular drift
part1.what: Thermophoretic force / drag must give the textbook free-molecular drift speed (derived independently from kinetic theory), up to the ~2.5% drag-model difference.

part1.name: Brownian motion: equipartition
part1.what: 2000 grains in dense gas for 10 drag times: thermal kicks plus drag must settle to <m v_x^2> = kT (fluctuation-dissipation).

part1.name: Spin-up and de-spin (time-dependent spin)
part1.what: A grain released during the yo-yo de-spin (4.8 Hz -> 1 rpm in 0.9 s; Coriolis, centrifugal and Euler forces) vs a 1e-12 ODE solution; a spinning grain must keep its absolute angular momentum while the payload spins up from 0 to 4.8 Hz in 3 s.
part1.value: error 0.10% of a 2.2 m path at dt = 0.5 ms, convergence ratio 4.00; |dL_abs|/L = 8.3e-12

part1.name: Release of wall-bound grains
part1.what: 300 grains settled on a tubule's aft face, with per-grain pull-off thresholds spread over ~2-1000 g: a steady 30 g pull (drag deceleration) and a 40 g, 200 Hz shaker burst must free exactly the grains whose JKR pull-off force 1.5 pi w R is exceeded; shaken grains leave at A w cos(phi), sin(phi) = a_th/(A w^2).
part1.value: steady pull: 112 of 112 expected; shaker: 137 of 137 expected, release speed error 2.0e-16 m/s

part1.name: Dust settles under the boost load
part1.what: 200 grains moving at 5 cm/s in a 0.5 x 0.5 x 1.5 in tubule under 25 g: within 0.4 s they must come to rest on the aft face (bounces that would return within one step are resting contacts), with none outside.
part1.value: 200/200 wall-bound, 200 on the aft face; safety-net corrections 0

part1.name: Re-entry deceleration (ballistic entry)
part1.what: The fall integrator with gravity off and an exponential atmosphere (H = 7 km), entering at 1.5 km/s at 90 and 45 degrees, vs Allen & Eggers (1958): v(h) = V exp(-rho H / (2 beta sin g)), peak deceleration V^2 sin g / (2 e H) at rho = beta sin g / H.
part1.value: peak deceleration within 1.2e-06, its altitude within 0.8 m, speed vs altitude within 6.0e-07

part2.name: 3-D contact dynamics vs the 1-D contact model
part2.what: Sticking speed of head-on impacts of two 50 um grains (silica, graphite): DEM bisection vs the 1-D JKR + damping integrator of contact.py.
part2.value: silica 6.186 vs 6.177 mm/s; graphite 38.344 vs 38.299 mm/s; worst 1.6e-03

part2.name: Momentum and energy in contact dynamics
part2.what: Oblique impact (impact parameter 0.25 diameters, 5 cm/s) of two spinning 50 um silica grains, no damping, no yield, sliding and rolling below their limits: linear and angular momentum through the impact, and the total energy (kinetic + JKR potential + sliding, rolling and twisting spring energy) over the whole time in contact.
part2.value: |dP|/P = 5.4e-15, |dL|/L = 1.6e-14, energy varies by 6.6e-07 of the impact energy over 293 samples in contact

part2.name: Rolling on a wall (plastic rolling)
part2.what: 50 um silica grain on borosilicate under 1 g pressing and a lateral body load ramped from 0 to 3x its rolling limit (4 F_c xi_crit / (m R), xi_crit = h a0/12, h = 0.5) in 2 ms: final speed vs the rigid-plastic rolling solution (m + I/R^2) dv/dt = m (a - a_roll) from the onset time, and rolling without slip (v = omega R).
part2.value: rolling limit 1.29 g; final speed 12.120 vs 12.081 mm/s (3.2e-03); slip 2.3e-08

part2.name: Statics of resting grains (sleep certificate)
part2.what: Stiffness of a grain on a wall from central differences of the production contact kernel vs the analytic JKR normal stiffness 1.2 E* a0 and Mindlin tangential k_t a0; static response to a 1 g sideways load: sliding force and rolling pseudo-force must both equal -m g.

part2.name: Random vibration synthesis (guide thrust axis)
part2.what: 20 s of the RockSat User Guide 2026 thrust-axis test spectrum (flat 0.051 g^2/Hz, 20-2000 Hz, 10.05 Grms) synthesised with Gaussian Fourier coefficients: Welch PSD (Hann, 8192 points) vs the spec over 40-1980 Hz, Grms, Gaussian moments, and the cubic-spline interpolant vs the exact band-limited signal between samples.
part2.value: PSD within 0.73 dB; Grms 10.031 vs 10.049; kurtosis 2.993; skewness 0.005; spline error 2.4e-06 sigma

part2.name: DEM time-step convergence
part2.what: Rolled distance of a 50 um silica grain on glass in 1 ms under twice its rolling limit, at the production step (~1/50 of the fastest contact period, 1.6e-8 s here) vs half of it.

part2.name: Slaved rolling vs full contact dynamics
part2.what: A grain on glass rolls past its limit and rocks under loads with 0.7, 2 and 3 kHz content (pressing load also oscillating), under 25 rad/s of payload spin spinning up at 40 rad/s^2 with the grain 0.7 m off the axis (centrifugal, Coriolis and Euler forces) and gas drag. roll1.py (stiff normal and sliding modes held quasi-static, rolling and twisting resolved at 1/200 of their period) vs the full-stiffness DEM at 10 ns.
part2.value: silica r = 50 um: path 624.416 um, difference 1.2e-05; graphite r = 25 um: path 165.552 um, difference 3.9e-06

part2.name: Sleeping grains do not miss motion
part2.what: A 50 um silica grain on glass under a sideways load ramped from 0 to 1.5x its rolling limit in 20 ms, integrated in the full model. While the engine's sleep certificate would hold (load <= 98% of the limit), the grain's displacement must equal the static deflection of its sliding and rolling springs (what the engine applies on waking it); afterwards it must roll.
part2.value: largest difference from the static deflection 0.047 nm (deflection up to 15.3 nm, xi_crit 15.6 nm); rolled 33.48 um by the end

part2.name: Free flight to contact hand-off (engine)
part2.what: Two silica grains (one spinning at 200 rad/s) approach obliquely at 5 cm/s, 40 um apart. The engine flies them exactly, hands them to the DEM within the capture distance, resolves the impact and lets them fly apart. Compared after 2 ms with the same initial state run in the DEM throughout (at half the engine's step): the engine may differ by no more than 3x the DEM's own step error (DEM at the engine's step vs half of it), i.e. the hand-off adds nothing beyond time discretisation.
part2.value: impacts 1; engine vs reference: velocity 4.4e-04, spin 4.1e-04, position 3.1e-04 of R; DEM step error: 4.0e-04, 5.1e-04, 2.8e-04

part2.name: Engine regimes vs all-DEM
part2.what: A row of 3 resting 50 um silica grains on a glass floor under 1 g, 6 um apart, struck end-on by a grain at 6 cm/s (the blow passes down the row); a grain rolling at 4 mm/s beside the row; a grain landing on the row from above at 1.5 cm/s; 5 more grains resting apart. Run 2 ms by the engine (sleepers join the DEM when approached, the rolling grain on the slaved model, flight exact, every step verified) and with every grain in the full DEM throughout (at the engine's step and at half of it). The engine may differ from the all-DEM run by no more than 3x the DEM's own step error, with the same contacts and outcomes.
part2.value: contacts: 5 (same in all runs: True); engine vs all-DEM: position 1.2e-03 R, velocity 4.2e-04 of 6 cm/s; DEM step error 8.8e-04 R, 6.2e-04; sleepers joined on approach 1, verified steps 2, steps redone 2
part2.criterion: same contacts; each <= 3x the step error

part2.name: Sleeping with the residual motion (linear response)
part2.what: Two touching 50 um silica grains on a glass floor under 1 g, the second nudged sideways at 0.2 mm/s, integrated 4 ms in the full model (still rocking and twisting). From that state: (a) 2 ms more of the full model; (b) the engine puts the pair to sleep with its residual motion as exact linear response (stiffness and dashpots from the kernel's tangent) and wakes it 2 ms later. (b) must match (a) to 5% of the residual itself (what dropping the residual would miss).
part2.value: engine vs full model: position 0.07 pm, spin 3.83e-05 rad/s; with the residual dropped: 936.61 pm, 1.89e-01 rad/s

part2.name: Slaved clusters vs full contact dynamics
part2.what: A stuck pair of 50 um silica grains on a glass floor, a grain stuck on top of another (leaning 20 deg) and a single grain, each driven past its rolling limit by a ramped sideways load with 0.7-3 kHz components under 25 rad/s of spin, integrated 2 ms by the slaved model (stiff modes quasi-static, 400 steps per softest period) and by the full model at 5 ns steps. Also reported: the slaving indicator the engine uses to accept a cluster (the shift of its soft frequencies; accepted at <= 2e-4, and <= 1e-3 when weighted by the loads' frequencies), which is conservative: the leaning grain is refused though its error is small.
part2.value: pair: path 8.06 um, difference 7.4e-06 (full model's own step error 6e-08; slaving indicator 2.1e-05, with the 3 kHz load 2.1e-05: accepted by the engine); tower: path 8.34 um, difference 1.7e-05 (full model's own step error 3e-07; slaving indicator 3.0e-04, with the 3 kHz load 1.9e-03: refused by the engine); single: path 8.15 um, difference 7.7e-06 (full model's own step error 1e-07; slaving indicator 2.1e-05, with the 3 kHz load 2.1e-05: accepted by the engine)
part2.criterion: <= 3e-5 of the rolled path, no hand-back

part2.name: Slaved clusters in the engine vs all-DEM
part2.what: A stuck pair of 50 um silica grains on a glass floor rolls sideways under 10 g (1 g pressing) while a single grain rolls after it, 0.4 mm behind and 10 cm/s faster, and hits it. Run 6 ms by the engine (the pair on the slaved model, the single grain on the slaved rolling model, both captured into the full model before they meet) and with every grain in the full model throughout (at the engine's step and half of it). Same contacts and outcomes; each grain within 3x the full model's own step error plus 3e-5 of its path (the slaved models' validated accuracy); slaved steps taken.
part2.value: contacts 5 (same as all-DEM: True); slaved entries 3, slaved grain-steps 8480; pair rolled 24.22 R; engine vs all-DEM 5.8e-06 R (allowed 4.8e-03-1.7e-02 R); DEM step error 5.5e-03 R; steps redone 3
part2.criterion: same contacts; slaved steps taken; each grain <= 3x step error + 3e-5 of its path
